first: अनृतं साहसं माया मूर्खत्वम् अतिलोभिता ।
en: Lying, rashness, trickery, foolishness, too much greed, uncleanliness and cruelty are faults said to be natural in women.

first: भोज्यं भोजनशक्तिश्च रतिशक्तिर्वराड्गना ।
en: Having good food and the power to digest it, desire and a lovely wife, wealth and the will to give it: these come only from great past merit.

first: यस्य पुत्रो वशीभूतो भार्या छन्दानुगामिनी ।
en: One whose son obeys him, whose wife follows his wishes, and who is content with what he has, finds heaven here on earth.

first: ते पुत्रा ये पितुर्भक्ताः स पिता यस्तु पोषकः ।
en: True sons are those devoted to their father; a true father is one who cares for them; a true friend is one you can trust; a true wife is one who brings peace.

first: परोक्षे कार्य्यहन्तारं प्रत्यक्षे प्रियवादिनम्॥
en: Avoid a friend who ruins your work behind your back and speaks sweetly to your face; he is like a pot of poison with milk on top.

first: न विश्वसेत्कुमित्रे च मित्रे चापि न विश्वसेत् ।
en: Do not trust a bad friend, and do not fully trust even a good friend; if he becomes angry one day, he may tell all your secrets.

first: मनसा चिन्तितं कार्यं वचसा न प्रकाशयेत् ।
en: Do not speak out a plan you have made in your mind; guard it closely like a secret and carry it out in action.

first: कष्टञ्च खलु मूर्खत्वं कष्टं च खलु यौवनम् ।
en: Foolishness is painful, and youth is painful too, but living in another person's house is the most painful of all.

first: शैले शैले न माणिक्यं मौक्तिकं न गजे गजे ।
en: Not every mountain has rubies, not every elephant has a pearl, not every forest has sandalwood, and good people are not found everywhere.

first: पुत्राश्च विविधैः शीलैर्नियोज्याः सततं बुधैः ।
en: Wise parents should always train their sons in good conduct; sons who know right ways and have good character are honoured by the family.

first: माता शत्रुः पिता वैरी येन बालो न पाठितः ।
en: A mother and father who do not educate their child are its enemies; such a child looks out of place in an assembly, like a crane among swans.

first: लालनाद् बहवो दोषास्ताडनाद् बहवो गुणाः ।
en: Spoiling brings many faults and discipline brings many virtues; so discipline a son or a pupil, and do not spoil him.

first: श्लोकेन वा तदर्ध्दाऽर्ध्दाक्षरेण वा ।
en: Make each day useful by learning a verse, half a verse, a quarter, or even one letter, and by giving and good deeds.

first: कान्ता वियोगः स्वजनापमानि ।
en: Separation from a loved wife, insults from one's own people, an unpaid debt, serving a bad king, poverty, and an unfair assembly burn the body without fire.

first: नदीतीरे च ये वृक्षाः परगेहेषु कामिनी ।
en: Trees on a river bank, a woman who lives in other men's houses, and kings without good advisers all perish quickly, without doubt.

first: बलं विद्या च विप्राणां राज्ञां सैन्यं बलं तथा ।
en: The strength of priests is learning, the strength of kings is their army, the strength of traders is wealth, and the strength of workers is service.

first: निर्धनं पुरुषं वेश्या प्रजा भग्नं नृपं त्यजेत् ।
en: A prostitute leaves a man who has no money, subjects leave a defeated king, birds leave a tree with no fruit, and a guest leaves a house after eating.

first: गृहीत्वा दक्षिणां विप्रास्त्यजन्ति यजमानकम् ।
en: Priests leave the patron once paid, a pupil leaves the teacher once he has learned, and deer leave a forest once it has burned.

first: दुराचारी दुरादृष्टिर्दुरावासी च दुर्जनः ।
en: A man who makes friends with someone of bad conduct, evil eyes, a bad place of living, or a wicked nature is soon ruined.

first: समाने शोभते प्रीतिः राज्ञि सेवा च शोभते ।
en: Friendship looks good between equals, service looks good under a king, trade looks good in business, and a good woman looks good in the home.
